cues.en: Thank you for coming. I'm Sandy Metz. I was a programmer for 35 years. I'm a woman of a certain age. I really am. I wrote a book a couple years ago. When it came out, it was like a bomb went off in my life. And I had to quit my day job. I was so busy doing other things. And because I quit my day job, I needed a way to make a living. And people kept asking me to teach, so I finally broke down and agreed to teach. To teach short object-oriented design classes.
cues.zh: 谢谢大家来。我是 Sandy Metz。我做了 35 年程序员。我是有一定年纪的女性。真的。几年前我写了一本书。书出版时，我的人生像炸了锅。我不得不辞掉正职。我忙着做其他事情。因为辞了正职，我需要一种谋生方式。人们不断请我去教书，所以我终于妥协，答应去教。教短期的面向对象设计课。

cues.en: And so then I had to make up curriculum. Boy, that was hard. Curriculum is tough. And so I sat down and I figured out what I thought were the most important set of lessons I could teach in three really intense days. And when I did that, when I made up the curriculum, I thought that they were all unrelated. I thought they were completely unrelated lessons. Good things, yes, but not the same thing.
cues.zh: 于是我得自己设计课程。天哪，太难了。设计课程真不容易。于是我坐下来，想清楚在三天非常高强度的课程里，我能教的最重要的一组课是什么。等我编完课程时，我以为它们彼此都无关。我以为这些课完全不相干。都是好东西，对，但不是同一回事。

cues.en: And then I've been teaching that course for the last year and a half, and I finally realized after, since now, actually, now my job is to think about code. What a wonderful thing. At this sort of advanced stage in my career, I'm not driven by deadline pressures every day. I really get to reflect about what makes code good and how we can make good code and how to explain to people how to do that. And so in the process of making this course, I've taught it over and over again, and I've got the leisure.
cues.zh: 后来在过去一年半里，我一直在教这门课，终于意识到——其实现在我的工作就是思考代码。多棒啊。在我职业生涯的这个进阶阶段，我不再每天被截止日期追着跑。我真的可以反思什么让代码变好、我们如何写出好代码，以及如何向别人解释怎么做。所以在制作这门课的过程中，我一遍又一遍地教它，也有了这份余裕。

cues.en: to reflect deeply about code. And I finally realized 18 months later that I wasn't really teaching a bunch of different ideas, that I was really teaching one idea, one simple idea. cues.en: And based on the result of that expression, one of the blocks, one of the following blocks is gonna get evaluated. cues.zh: 根据这个表达式的结果，会执行其中一个代码块，也就是下面这些代码块中的一个。如果求值为 true，我就会执行 else 这个词前面的代码块。如果求值为 false，我就会执行 else 这个词后面的代码块。所以这其实就是这个意思，对吧？但在 Ruby 里实际上会稍微复杂一点，因为我们有 truthy 这个概念。

cues.en: If it's truthy, I'm going to evaluate the code before the else, the block of code before the else. Otherwise, I'm going to evaluate the block of code after the else. This is a type check. And we don't do type checks in OO. We hate this idea. I don't want to have the syntax. I just want to send a message to an object.
cues.zh: 如果它是真值，我就执行 else 前面那段代码；否则，我就执行 else 后面的代码。这就是类型检查。而在面向对象里我们不做类型检查，我们讨厌这个想法。我不想要这种语法，我只想给对象发消息。

cues.en: I don't want to have to look at the kind of thing it is and make a decision and then choose between two different kinds of behavior. If you came to Ruby and OO from a procedural language like most of us did, it probably seemed normal and reasonable to write long conditions and start with if or case or whatever. But I can promise you that the very presence of this keyword in our language makes it easy to retain that procedural mindset.
cues.zh: 我不想非得先看它是什么类型、做个判断，然后在两种不同行为之间选一个。如果你是像我们大多数人一样，从过程式语言转到 Ruby 和面向对象的，那么写长长的条件、用 if 或 case 之类开头，可能看起来很正常、很合理。但我可以向你保证，这个关键字只要出现在我们的语言里，就很容易让人保留那种过程式思维。

cues.en: And it keeps you from learning OO and taking advantage of the power of objects. And to show you how unnecessary this keyword is, let's just change Ruby to have small talk-like syntax for dealing with conditions. Message sending syntax. Here we go. cues.zh: 而且它会让你没法学习面向对象，也没法利用对象的能力。为了说明这个关键字有多没必要，我们干脆把 Ruby 改成类似 Smalltalk 的语法来处理条件。消息发送语法。开始吧。首先我们得打开 TrueClass，因为我确定这不会有问题。

cues.en: And so I'm going to implement an API. The API is these two messages. I'm going to do if true and if false. So in true class, the if true method, now I'm taking advantage of the fact that all these methods take an implicit block. The if true method in true class is going to yield to the block. Now I'm going to return self, just ignore that for now. It'll be clear later while we did it. The if false method, if false is implementation, true class does nothing. It does not yield to the block.
cues.zh: 所以我要实现一个 API。这个 API 就是这两条消息。我要做 if true 和 if false。那么在 TrueClass 里，if true 方法——现在我利用的是所有这些方法都接收一个隐式代码块这一点。TrueClass 里的 if true 方法会 yield 给代码块。然后我要返回 self，先别管这个。之后我们做的时候就会明白为什么。if false 方法，if false 的实现是：TrueClass 什么都不做。它不会 yield 给代码块。

cues.en: And so then once you see that, you can pretty much guess what has to go in false class. It's just the opposite. True's going to yield in the if true method. If I got a true, remember that if true does the yield, so it'll evaluate the block. If I send that message to a true, if I send that same message to a false, nothing happens.

cues.zh: 我要让这些 data 方法尽可能完全一样。所以首先，我得把那个从里面拿出来。我就把它放进去。我会把实际数组放进一个常量里。我会实现 data 方法，只用来返回它。所以如果我看下面那个东西，现在就可以继续做变换，比如。我可以把那个放到那里。没必要，但可行。我还可以把底部的 super 去掉，换成 data。现在，还是有点难把握这个概念，但已经更容易看出哪里变了。我们得弄清楚那个东西是什么，并给它起个名字。

cues.en: And I was lucky enough to teach with Obdy Grimm in the fall, and he suggested to the students who are dealing with this problem that we pretend it's rows and columns in a spreadsheet. Write them down like this, and then label every column. What is the header of the column? Well, that's the class. I suck at names, so let's call that data. The interesting question here is, what is this? And we call the subclass Random House, but this is not random. Random is an instance of whatever this thing is.
cues.zh: 秋季我有幸和 Obdy Grimm 一起授课，他建议遇到这个问题的学生，把它想象成电子表格里的行和列。像这样写下来，然后给每一列加上标签。这一列的表头是什么？嗯，那就是类。我不擅长起名，所以就叫它 data。这里有趣的问题是，这是什么？我们把这个子类叫作 Random House，但它并不是随机的。Random 是这个东西的实例。

cues.en: All right? What is it? It's order. OK, I see these guys. You're like too nerdly. That's your problem. Too much nerd cred. The thing that we're changing is order. And so if order is that thing, then this is not nothing. This is an algorithm. And it's just as valid as the other one. And so now that you know its name, if you ask order as a hassle, that is so clearly wrong. That is absolutely wrong. Order is a roll.
cues.zh: 好吗？它是什么？是顺序。好，我看到这些家伙了。你们有点太技术宅了。这就是你们的问题。极客声望太重了。我们要改变的东西是顺序。所以如果顺序就是那个东西，那这可不是无关紧要。这是一种算法。它和另一个一样成立。所以现在你知道它的名字了，如果你把顺序当成麻烦，那就明显错了。那绝对错了。顺序就是规则。

cues.en: And so let's write the order rules. Here's one. I'm going to make random house. I'm going to call the API order. I'll have it take an argument. That's the array. And it's going to shuffle it. What's the implementation here? Yeah. It's an algorithm. It's real. And so if I want to use this, I'm just going to throw it. Let's throw that subclass away. That didn't help. That went badly wrong. I'm just going to move this code around. I'll put an adder reader in for data.
cues.zh: 那么，我们来写排序规则。这里有一个。我要创建一个 RandomHouse。我要调用 API order。让它接收一个参数，也就是这个数组，然后把它打乱。这里的实现是什么？对，这是一个算法，真的。所以如果我想用它，我就直接把它扔进去。把这个子类扔掉吧。那没帮上忙。那错得很离谱。我就把这段代码挪一挪。我会给数据放一个 adder reader。

cues.en: And you know what's in that, so we can get rid of that. I need the space. So I'm just going to remove the responsibility for ordering that array from house. I'm going to do it by using this order. So I'm going to inject it. It's a name parameter. I'm going to inject an order. And I'm going to give that order an opportunity to order the data. And it's whatever it does is what house is going to have. And it works. So what have I just done? Well, I got more code.
cues.zh: 你知道里面有什么，所以我们可以把它去掉。我需要腾出空间。所以我要把给那个数组排序的职责从 house 中移除。我会用这个 order 来做。所以我要把它注入进来。它是一个 name 参数。我要注入一个 order。然后我会给这个 order 一个机会来给数据排序。它怎么做，house 就会得到什么。而且它奏效了。那我刚才做了什么？嗯，我多了些代码。

cues.en: to do exactly the same thing. And this is why people complain about object-oriented design, right? Because they can't think further ahead than this. But watch this. I got these, too, right? I got another kind of order. Why don't I just inject that instead? And that just works. This is composition. We're trying to inject an object to play the role of the thing that varies. How are we going to do echo house? You totally know. You see the answer to this problem already, right? I need something to do this.
cues.zh: 去做完全相同的事。这就是人们抱怨面向对象设计的原因，对吧？因为他们没法想得更远。但看这个。我也有这些，对吧？我有另一种 order。那我为什么不直接注入它呢？而这就直接能用了。这就是组合。我们是想注入一个对象，让它扮演那个会变化的东西的角色。那我们要怎么做 echo house？你完全知道。你已经看到这个问题的答案了，对吧？我需要一个东西来做这件事。

cues.en: And then I need another thing to play another variant of this role. And if I have these things, I'm going to inject them. We love dependency injection. I'm going to put this up. OK, wait. Here, I have to do that again. Sorry. It's got to line up. It kills me. So I'm going to keep the formula. And I'm going to stick it way down here because I want to intervene in the most narrow part possible. Your mileage may vary. But I put it there when I wrote this code.
cues.zh: 然后我还需要另一个东西来扮演这个角色的另一个变体。如果我有这些东西，我就会把它们注入进去。我们喜欢依赖注入。我要把这个放上去。好，等等。这里我得再来一次，抱歉。它必须对齐，这真要命。所以我会保留这个公式。然后我会把它放到很下面，因为我想在尽可能窄的部分介入。效果可能因人而异。但我写这段代码时就是把它放在那里。

cues.en: All right? And so now, again, I have exactly the same behavior I had before I created these two new objects and injected them. But I can also inject the other one. And now I got echo house. So I have defined two roles, and they each have two players. And so instead of getting line 12, let's just recite the whole thing. So here's the set of things I can do, right? I can get house. I can get random house. I can get echo house. Or I can get random echo house.
cues.zh: 可以吧？那么现在，我得到的行为，和我在创建并注入这两个新对象之前完全一样。但我也可以注入另一个。现在我就得到了 echo house。所以我定义了两个角色，每个角色各有两个玩家。所以与其只看第 12 行，不如把整套都过一遍。这就是我能做的一组操作，对吧？我可以拿到 house。我可以拿到 random house。我可以拿到 echo house。或者我可以拿到 random echo house。

cues.en: and we have not, we no longer have more code, we have actually less code, and there is not one bit of duplication in here. We've made this units of pluggable behavior. Before when it was inheritance, it looked like this, but really what we want, if there's a specialization, there's, by definition, there is never just one specialization. The new thing is one thing, but the old thing that you specialize is something, even if it looks like nothing. So you have to isolate the thing that varies. You have to figure out what it is.
cues.zh: 而且我们并没有——我们不再有更多代码，实际上代码更少了，这里没有一点重复。我们把这些做成了可插拔行为的单元。以前用继承时，它看起来是这样；但我们真正想要的是，如果有特化，按定义就绝不会只有一个特化。新东西是一个东西，但你特化的旧东西也是某个东西，哪怕它看起来什么都不是。所以你必须隔离变化的部分。你必须弄清楚它到底是什么。

cues.en: And that leaves a hole in house where you have to plug that stuff back in. Then you've got to figure out what its name is. Here we call them order and format. You have to define that role. We made APIs for the order and formatter. And then later at runtime, somebody is going to inject the player. Here, wait. Let's see that again, too. Sorry. I love it. It is really one of the few consolations in making talks, keynote effects. So this is composition plus dependency injection. And this is what it means to do object-oriented design.
cues.zh: 这样就在房子里留下一个洞，你得把那些东西重新插回去。然后你得弄清楚它叫什么名字。这里我们称它们为 order 和 format。你必须定义这个角色。我们为 order 和 formatter 做了 API。然后稍后在运行时，会有人把 player 注入进来。等等。我们再看一遍。抱歉。我喜欢这个。它确实是做演讲时为数不多的慰藉之一：keynote 效果。所以这就是组合加依赖注入。而这就是面向对象设计的含义。

cues.en: All right. Understanding these techniques lets you find the underlying abstraction. And getting that extraction right is going to dramatically improve your code. If you're talking to nil, it's something. Use the null object pattern. You're done checking for nil. OK? Stop it right now. Make objects to stand in for those nils and use those active nothings. Next, beware of inheritance. It's easy to begin with. And maybe you should use it to start with.
cues.zh: 好。理解这些技巧，能让你找到底层抽象。而把这个提取做对，会大幅提升你的代码。如果你在跟 nil 打交道，那说明有情况。用空对象模式。你就不用再检查 nil 了。明白吗？立刻停下。创建对象来替代那些 nil，并使用这些主动的空对象。接下来，小心继承。它一开始很容易。也许你一开始就该用它。

cues.en: but it's a knife that will turn in your hand, especially if the amount of code that you specialize is a small proportion of the class that you're subclassing. Be very careful if you use it and be ready to switch to composition. It's not for sharing behavior.
cues.zh: 但它是一把会反噬你的刀，尤其当你特化的代码只占所继承类的一小部分时。使用时要非常小心，并准备好改用组合。它不是用来共享行为的。

cues.en: The bigger idea as we move out in scale here is there's no such thing as one specialization. When you see that you have a variant, it means that you have two. And you have to isolate the thing that varies, name that concept, define the role, and then inject the players. When you got started in OO, when you first started writing OO, it was really easy to see that real things could be modeled as objects, right? The chair that you're sitting on, the chair that you're in, the person beside you.
cues.zh: 随着我们在尺度上向外扩展，更大的想法是：不存在所谓的单一特化。当你看到一个变体时，意味着你其实有两个。你必须隔离变化的东西，给这个概念命名，定义角色，然后注入参与者。刚接触 OO、刚开始写 OO 时，很容易看出现实事物可以建模为对象，对吧？你坐着的椅子，你所在的椅子，你旁边的人。

cues.en: And it didn't take long when she started writing code to figure out that more abstract things could be modeled usefully, right? Business rules, ideas, concepts, processes. And back in the beginning of this talk, I started with fixed nums and Booleans. And you might not have really thought, we're so used to those ideas that you don't really think of them as being abstractions, but they are not real. You cannot reach out and pick up a six or a true, right? But inside my app, that six and the true are as real as the chair.
cues.zh: 当她开始写代码后，没过多久就发现，更抽象的东西也能被有效地建模，对吧？业务规则、想法、概念、流程。回到这场演讲的开头，我从固定数字和布尔值讲起。你可能没真正想过——我们太习惯这些概念了，以至于不觉得它们是抽象——但它们并不真实。你没法伸手拿起一个 6 或一个 true，对吧？但在我的应用里，那个 6 和那个 true 就和椅子一样真实。

cues.en: Now, numbers are an amazing abstraction, but then there's a way that the abstraction in numbers doubles up, and that's with zero. We didn't have zero for a really long time. Zero represented nothing. And before we had the idea of zero, there were things we couldn't do. And then after we had the idea of zero, that concept became a polymorphic.
cues.zh: 现在，数字是一种了不起的抽象，但数字里的抽象还有一层叠加，那就是零。我们很久都没有零。零代表无。在我们有零这个概念之前，有些事我们做不到。后来有了零的概念，这个概念就变成了多态的。

cues.en: in our terms, right? We could use numbers in new ways once we discovered that the nothing in the number set could be represented by the symbol zero. So your applications are full of things like zero, right? There are concepts that are abstractions that reveal their presence by the absence of code.
cues.zh: 用我们的说法，对吧？一旦我们发现数字集合中的“无”可以用符号零表示，我们就能以新的方式使用数字。所以你的应用里到处都是像零这样的东西，对吧？有些概念是抽象，它们通过代码的缺席来显露自身的存在。

cues.en: I don't want to write a condition. I just want to send a message to an object. And if you want to do OO that way, you have to find those objects. And they're hidden in the spaces between the lines in your code. They seem like nothing, but they aren't. They're actually something always. It's true that they're something because something, nothing is always something. Thank you. I'm Sandy Metz buzzing at me. Am I in a new book?
